title: The Heavenly Voice Warns Kansa
one_line_summary: A voice from the sky warns Kansa that the eighth child of Devaki will kill him; he draws his sword but Vasudeva persuades him to spare her in exchange for surrendering every child she bears.
source_excerpt: As they were going along, a voice in the sky, sounding aloud and deep as thunder, addressed Kansa, and said, "Fool that you are, the eighth child of the damsel whom you are driving in the car shall take away your life!" On hearing this, Kansa drew his sword, and was about to put Devakí to death; but Vasudeva interposed.

title: Earth Petitions the Gods and Vishnu Promises to Descend
one_line_summary: Overburdened Earth appeals to the gods at mount Meru; Brahmá leads them to the milky sea, where Vishnu plucks a black and a white hair and vows to incarnate as Devaki's eighth child to relieve her.
source_excerpt: the supreme lord plucked off two hairs, one white and one black, and said to the gods, "These my hairs shall descend upon earth, and shall relieve her of the burden of her distress... This my (black) hair shall be impersonated in the eighth conception of the wife of Vasudeva, Devakí... and shall slay Kansa, who is the demon Kálanemi."

title: Kansa Imprisons Vasudeva and Devaki
one_line_summary: Nárada tells Kansa that Vishnu will be Devaki's eighth child; enraged, Kansa confines Vasudeva and Devaki, and Vasudeva delivers each of the first six infants to him as promised.
source_excerpt: The Muni Nárada informed Kansa that the supporter of the earth, Vishńu, would be the eighth child of Devakí; and his wrath being excited by this report, he placed both Vasudeva and Devakí in confinement.

title: Vishnu Instructs Yoganidrá on the Exchange of the Infants
one_line_summary: Vishnu charges Yoganidrá to convey six demon embryos into Devaki's womb, to transfer the seventh (Sesha) to Rohini, and to be born herself as Yashoda's daughter to be dashed by Kansa and ascend as a goddess.
source_excerpt: To her Vishńu said, "Go, Nidrá, to the nether regions, and by my command conduct successively six of their princes to be conceived of Devakí... I will myself become incarnate in the eighth conception of Devakí; and you shall immediately take a similar character as the embryo offspring of Yaśodá."

title: The Conception of Devaki
one_line_summary: Yoganidrá conveys the six embryos into Devaki's womb and transfers the seventh to Rohini; Hari then becomes incarnate as Devaki's conception while Yoganidrá enters Yashoda's, and the gods hymn the radiant mother.
source_excerpt: conveyed the six several embryos into the womb of Devakí, and transferred the seventh after a season to that of Rohińí; after which, Hari, for the benefit of the three regions, became incarnate as the conception of the former princess, and Yoganidrá as that of Yaśodá.

title: The Birth of Krishna
one_line_summary: At midnight Devaki gives birth to the four-armed lotus-eyed child bearing the Śrívatsa mark; at the entreaty of Vasudeva and Devaki he withholds his divine form and appears as an ordinary infant.
source_excerpt: As soon as Ánakadundubhi beheld the child, of the complexion of the lotus leaves, having four arms, and the mystic mark Śrívatsa on his breast, he addressed him in terms of love and reverence, and represented the fears he entertained of Kansa.

title: Vasudeva Carries Krishna across the Yamuna
one_line_summary: The prison guards charmed by Yoganidrá, Vasudeva bears the infant across the flooded Yamuna, sheltered by Sesha's hoods, and exchanges him for Yashoda's newborn daughter in Gokula.
source_excerpt: To protect the infant from the heavy rain that fell from the clouds of night, Śesha, the many-headed serpent, followed Vasudeva, and spread his hoods above their heads; and when the prince... crossed the Yamuná river... the waters were stilled, and rose not above his knee.

title: Kansa Dashes the Infant Girl Who Becomes Yoganidrá
one_line_summary: Kansa seizes Devaki's child and hurls her against a stone; she rises into the sky as an eight-armed goddess who warns him that his destroyer is already born, then vanishes.
source_excerpt: he threw it ruthlessly against a stone; but it rose into the sky, and expanded into a gigantic figure, having eight arms, each wielding some formidable weapon... "he is born who shall kill thee, the mighty one amongst the gods, who was formerly thy destroyer."

title: Kansa Orders the Slaughter of Children and the Pious
one_line_summary: Realising his slayer has escaped, Kansa summons his Asuras, orders every boy of unusual vigour to be slain and all liberal sacrificers put to death, then releases Vasudeva and Devaki.
source_excerpt: Let therefore active search be made for whatever young children there may be upon earth, and let every boy in whom there are signs of unusual vigour be slain without remorse.

title: Nanda Brings the Infants Home to Gokula
one_line_summary: Set at liberty, Vasudeva bids Nanda take both Krishna and Balarama to Gokula to be reared as his own sons; Nanda and the cowherds return with their waggons.
source_excerpt: let this boy, the son whom Rohińí has borne me, accompany you, and be brought up by you as this your own son. Accordingly Nanda and the other cowherds... returned to their village.

title: Krishna Slays the Demoness Putana
one_line_summary: The child-killer Putana comes by night and suckles the infant Krishna, who drains her of her life; the terrified cowherds find the vast carcass and Nanda and Yashoda shield the child with prayers.
source_excerpt: the female fiend Pútaná, the child-killer, came thither by night, and finding the little Krishńa asleep, took him up, and gave him her breast to suck... but Krishńa... sucked it with such violence, that he drained it of the life.

title: Krishna Overturns the Waggon
one_line_summary: The sleeping infant Krishna kicks over the waggon beneath which he lies, scattering and breaking the pots; the astonished cowherds credit the boys' account that the child alone did it.
source_excerpt: whilst Madhusúdana was asleep underneath the waggon, he cried for the breast, and kicking up his feet he overturned the vehicle, and all the pots and pans were upset and broken.

title: Garga Names Rama and Krishna
one_line_summary: The sage Garga, sent secretly by Vasudeva, performs the initiatory rites for the two boys and names the elder Ráma and the other Krishńa.
source_excerpt: The initiatory rites requisite for the two boys were performed by Garga, who was sent to Gokula by Vasudeva for that purpose... and named the elder of them Ráma, and the other Krishńa.

title: Krishna Fells the Two Arjuna Trees
one_line_summary: Yashoda ties Krishna to a wooden mortar; he drags it between two Arjuna trees and pulls them crashing down, from which deed he is called Dámodara.
source_excerpt: Fastening a cord round his waist, she tied him to the wooden mortar... the lotus-eyed Krishńa... pulled the mortar after him to the space between two Arjuna trees... and as Krishńa pulled it through, it pulled down the trunks of the trees... It is hence that Krishńa is called Dámodara.

title: The Cowherds Migrate to Vrindavana
one_line_summary: Alarmed by the death of Putana, the upset waggon, and the fallen trees, the elders of Vraja resolve to leave and move the whole settlement to Vrindavana.
source_excerpt: The elders of the cowherds, with Nanda at their head... said they... 'We cannot remain in this place... let us go to Vrindávana, where terrestrial prodigies may no more disturb us.'

title: Krishna Leaps into Kaliya's Pool
one_line_summary: Krishna climbs a Kadamba tree and plunges into the venomous pool of the serpent Kaliya; the coiling snakes bite him and his stricken parents and companions rush to the bank in despair.
source_excerpt: he bound his clothes tightly about him, and jumped boldly into the lake of the serpent-king... Coiling themselves around Krishńa, they all bit him with teeth from which fiery poison was emitted.

title: Krishna Dances on Kaliya and Banishes Him
one_line_summary: Reminded of his divinity by Balarama, Krishna tramples Kaliya's heads in a triumphant dance, then spares the pleading serpent on condition that he leave the Yamuna for the ocean.
source_excerpt: Laying hold of the middle hood of their chief with both his hands, he bent it down, and set his foot upon the hitherto unbended head, and danced upon it in triumph... So saying, Hari set the snake-king at liberty, who... departed to the ocean.

title: Rama Destroys the Ass-Demon Dhenuka
one_line_summary: In the palm grove, the demon Dhenuka in ass form kicks at Rama, who seizes him by the hind legs, whirls him to death, and hurls the carcass into a palm tree; his kin are slain likewise.
source_excerpt: Ráma, however, seized him by both hind legs, and whirling him round until he expired, tossed his carcass to the top of a palm tree... The animals that were of kin to Dhenuka came running to his aid; but Krishńa and Ráma treated them in the same manner.

title: Rama Destroys the Asura Pralamba
one_line_summary: Disguised as a cowherd, the Asura Pralamba joins the boys' game and carries off Balarama; reminded by Krishna of his true self, Balarama crushes the demon to death.
source_excerpt: the powerful Baladeva laughed, and squeezed Pralamba with his knees, striking him at the same time on the head and face with his fists, so as to beat out both his eyes... fell upon the ground, and expired.

title: Krishna Questions the Worship of Indra
one_line_summary: When Nanda explains the annual sacrifice to Indra, Krishna argues that forest-dwellers should worship cattle and the mountain Govarddhana instead of the king of the celestials.
source_excerpt: We, father, are neither cultivators of the soil, nor dealers in merchandise; we are sojourners in forests, and cows are our divinities... Let prayer and offerings then be addressed to the mountain Govarddhana.

title: The Villagers Worship Govarddhana
one_line_summary: Persuaded by Krishna, the cowherds offer curds, milk and flesh to the mountain, feed the Brahmans, and circumambulate the cattle; Krishna himself appears on the summit saying 'I am the mountain'.
source_excerpt: Upon the summit of Govarddhana, Krishńa presented himself, saying, "I am the mountain," and partook of much food presented by the Gopas.

title: Indra Unlooses the Storm upon Gokula
one_line_summary: Angered at the loss of his offerings, Indra commands the Samvarttaka clouds to deluge the cattle with rain and wind, and the torrents overwhelm the frightened settlement.
source_excerpt: Now, therefore, afflict the cattle, that are their sustenance, and whence their occupation is derived, with rain and wind... In an instant the earth, the points of the horizon, and the sky, were all blended into one by the heavy and incessant shower.

title: Krishna Lifts Govarddhana for Seven Days
one_line_summary: Krishna plucks up the mountain Govarddhana and holds it aloft as a vast umbrella, sheltering the people and cattle for seven days until Indra calls off the storm.
source_excerpt: Krishńa immediately plucked up the mountain Govarddhana, and held it aloft with one hand in sport... For seven days and nights did the vast clouds sent by Indra rain upon the Gokula of Nanda... but they were protected by the elevation of the mountain.

title: Indra Installs Krishna as Govinda
one_line_summary: Indra descends on Airávata, praises Krishna for saving the cattle, and by the wish of the kine installs him as Upendra, declaring he shall be called Govinda.
source_excerpt: I have now come by desire of the cattle, grateful for their preservation, in order to install you as Upendra; and, as the Indra of the cows, thou shalt be called Govinda.

title: Krishna Promises to Befriend Arjuna
one_line_summary: Indra asks Krishna to protect Arjuna, born as a portion of himself, and Krishna vows to defend him in battle and restore Kunti's sons after the Bhárata war.
source_excerpt: A portion of me has been born as Arjuna, the son of Pritha: let him ever be defended by thee... To this Krishńa replied, "I know thy son... and I will befriend him as long as I continue upon earth."

title: The Cowherds Wonder at Krishna
one_line_summary: The cowherds, having seen Kaliya subdued, Pralamba killed and Govarddhana lifted, question who Krishna truly is; he answers simply that he is their kinsman.
source_excerpt: Assuredly we repose at the feet of Hari... for, having witnessed thy power, we cannot believe thee to be a man... Krishna replied, '...be satisfied to know that I am your kinsman. I am neither god, nor Yaksha, nor Gandharba, nor Dánava.'

title: The Rasa Dance with the Gopis
one_line_summary: On a moonlit autumn night Krishna and the Gopis join in the Rasa dance; the women, drawn from their homes, imitate his sports and circle him in love and devotion.
source_excerpt: Krishńa thought the lovely moonlight night of autumn propitious to the Rasa dance... Then proceeded the dance to the music of their clashing bracelets, and songs that celebrated in suitable strain the charms of the autumnal season.

title: Krishna Slays the Bull-Demon Arishta
one_line_summary: The demon Arishta in the form of a savage bull charges Krishna, who seizes him by the horns, wrings his throat, and beats him to death with his own torn horn.
source_excerpt: he seized him as an alligator would have done, and held him firmly by the horns, whilst he pressed his sides with his knees... and then tearing off one of the horns, he beat the fierce demon with it until he died.

title: Narada Reveals the Boys to Kansa
one_line_summary: Nárada tells Kansa the whole history of the child's transference from Devaki to Yashoda; Kansa rebukes Vasudeva and resolves to destroy Krishna and Rama while they are still young.
source_excerpt: Nárada went to Kansa, and related to him the whole, beginning with the transference of the child from Devakí to Yaśodá... Kansa was highly incensed with Vasudeva, and bitterly reproached him, and all the Yádavas.

title: Kansa Dispatches Akrura to Fetch the Boys
one_line_summary: Kansa plans to lure Krishna and Rama to a boxing festival, sends Kesin to attack them, and orders the Yadu Akrura to bring the two cowherd boys to Mathura.
source_excerpt: I will send the noble Yadu, Akrúra the son of Swaphalka, to Gokula, to bring them hither: I will order the fierce Keśin... to attack them... my elephant Kuvalayápíd́a shall trample to death these two cow-boy sons of Vasudeva.

title: Krishna Slays the Horse-Demon Kesin
one_line_summary: The demon Kesin attacks in the form of a great steed; Krishna thrusts his arm into its mouth and rends it asunder, and Nárada declares he shall henceforth be called Kesava.
source_excerpt: Krishńa enlarging the bulk of his arm, thrust it into his mouth, and wrenched out the teeth... The formidable demon, having his mouth rent open by the arm of Krishńa, fell down, torn asunder like a tree struck by lightning... thou shalt be known in the world by the name of Keśava.

title: Akrura Beholds the Divine Youths
one_line_summary: Filled with devotion, Akrura journeys to Gokula and, arriving at milking-time, beholds the radiant Krishna and Balabhadra among the cattle.
source_excerpt: he saw Krishńa amongst the cattle, dark as the leaf of the full blown lotus... Akrúra also beheld there Balabhadra, white as a jasmine, a swan, or the moon... When Akrúra saw these two youths, his countenance expanded with delight.

title: Krishna Vows to Slay Kansa within Three Nights
one_line_summary: Akrura tells Krishna of the insults suffered by Vasudeva, Devaki and Ugrasena, and of Kansa's purpose; Krishna promises to go to Mathura and slay Kansa and his adherents within three nights.
source_excerpt: Akúra told them how their father Ánakadundubhi... had been insulted by the iniquitous demon Kansa... The destroyer of Keśin said to him, '...Within three nights I will slay Kansa and his adherents.'

title: The Gopis Lament the Departure
one_line_summary: As Krishna and Rama prepare to leave for Mathura, the Gopis weep and grieve that the city women will win their Hari, and watch the chariot's dust vanish.
source_excerpt: The Gopís, seeing them about to set forth, were much afflicted; they wept bitterly... 'Alas! alas! we see now only the dust of his chariot wheels! and now he is far away, for even that dust is no longer to be seen!'

title: Akrura Sees the Divine Forms in the Yamuna
one_line_summary: Bathing in the Yamuna, Akrura beholds Balarama as the thousand-hooded serpent and Krishna as four-armed Vishnu, then finds them again seated humanly in the chariot and hymns the deity.
source_excerpt: he beheld mentally Balabhadra, having a thousand hooded beads... On his lap he also beheld... Krishńa, of the complexion of a cloud... armed with the discus and other weapons... Apprehending, therefore, their real character, he thus eulogized the eternal deity.

title: Krishna Slays the Insolent Washerman
one_line_summary: Entering Mathura, Krishna and Rama take fine clothes from Kansa's washerman; when he abuses them, Krishna strikes him down and kills him, and the two don the garments.
source_excerpt: The washerman was the servant of Kansa, made insolent by his master's favour; and he provoked the two lads with loud and scurrilous abuse, until Krishńa struck him down, with his head to the ground, and killed him.

title: Krishna Blesses the Flower-Seller
one_line_summary: A humble flower-seller honours the two youths and gives them choice flowers; pleased, Krishna grants him lasting fortune, vigour, and a heavenly abode.
source_excerpt: Krishńa then, being much pleased with him, gave him this blessing; "Fortune, good friend, who depends upon me, shall never forsake you... you shall finally obtain... a heavenly region, the consequence of my favour."

title: Krishna Straightens the Hunchback Kubja
one_line_summary: Krishna asks the crooked Kubja for her unguent, anoints himself and Rama, then by pressing her head and feet makes her straight and beautiful; grateful, she invites him to her house.
source_excerpt: Then Krishńa, skilled in the curative art, took hold of her, under the chin, with the thumb and two fingers, and lifted up her head, whilst with his feet he pressed down her feet; and in this way he made her straight.

title: Krishna Breaks the Great Bow
one_line_summary: In the hall of arms Krishna takes up the bow set for the trial, bends it and snaps it in two, filling Mathura with the sound; he and Rama defy the angry warders.
source_excerpt: he took it, and bent it; but drawing it with violence, he snapped it in two, and all Mathurá resounded with the noise which its fracture occasioned.

title: The Youths Slay the Elephant Kuvalayapida
one_line_summary: Goaded upon them at the arena gate, Kansa's elephant Kuvalayapida attacks Krishna and Rama, who slay it and enter the arena armed with its tusks.
source_excerpt: Covered with must and blood from the elephant, whom, when goaded upon them by his driver, they had slain, and armed with his tusks, Balabhadra and Janárddana confidently entered the arena.

title: Krishna and Balarama Kill the Wrestlers
one_line_summary: In the arena Krishna whirls Chanura and dashes him to death, while Balarama crushes Mushtika; the other wrestlers flee as the two dance victorious.
source_excerpt: Having whirled Cháńúra round a hundred times... Krishńa dashed him on the ground with such violence as to smash his body into a hundred fragments... the mighty Baladeva... pummelled him there till he was dead.

title: Krishna Slays Kansa
one_line_summary: Enraged by Kansa's orders to kill his kin, Krishna springs upon the throne, seizes the king by the hair, and crushes him to death; Balarama slays his brother Sumalin.
source_excerpt: springing up to the place where he was seated, laid hold of him by the hair of his head, and struck his tiara to the ground: then casting him down upon the earth, Govinda threw himself upon him. Crushed by the weight of the upholder of the universe... Kansa the king, gave up the ghost.

title: Krishna Bows to Vasudeva and Devaki
one_line_summary: After slaying Kansa, Krishna and Balarama embrace the feet of Vasudeva and Devaki, who recall his words at birth and acknowledge him as the lord of the universe.
source_excerpt: Krishńa, accompanied by Balabhadra, embraced the feet of Vasudeva and of Devakí... recalling to recollection what he had said to them at his birth, they bowed to Janárddana.

title: Krishna Places Ugrasena on the Throne
one_line_summary: Krishna consoles Kansa's grieving wives, liberates Ugrasena from confinement, and crowns him king of Mathura, offering him the service of the Yadava race.
source_excerpt: The foe of Madhu then liberated Ugrasena from confinement, and placed him on the throne, which the death of his son had left vacant... performed the funeral rites of Kansa.

title: Krishna Obtains the Celestial Hall Sudharman
one_line_summary: Krishna bids Vayu ask Indra to resign the splendid hall Sudharman; Indra yields it, and the Yadava chiefs thenceforth possess the jewel-adorned celestial court.
source_excerpt: Go, Váyu, to Indra, and desire him to lay aside his pomp, and resign to Ugrasena his splendid hall Sudharman... Indra... immediately gave up to him the hall Sudharman.
variant_notes: VARIANT of the Sudharman-hall motif: Vishnu Purana 5.21 tells the fetching of the celestial hall for Ugrasena at Mathura; Harivamsha 1.115 folds the same hall into the enrichment of Dwaraka. Different placement — kept separate.

title: Krishna Studies under Sandipani and Recovers His Son
one_line_summary: Krishna and Rama master all arms under the sage Sandipani in sixty-four days; as his fee they plunge into the sea, slay the conch-demon Panchajana, and restore the teacher's drowned son.
source_excerpt: having slain the vile Panchajana, he took the conch shell... The heroes also recovered the boy from the pains of death, and restored him in his former person to his father.

title: Jarasandha Besieges Mathura
one_line_summary: Angered at Kansa's death, Jarasandha of Magadha invests Mathura with a vast host; armed with celestial weapons, Krishna and Balarama rout him, and defeat his renewed attacks eighteen times.
source_excerpt: Eighteen times did the haughty prince of Magadhá renew his attack upon the Yádavas, headed by Krishńa; and was as often defeated and put to the rout by them, with very inferior numbers.

title: The Rise of Kalayavana
one_line_summary: Insulted by the Yadavas, the Brahman Gargya performs penance and obtains a son, Kalayavana, who demands of Narada the mightiest heroes and marches with a vast host against Mathura.
source_excerpt: Śyála having called Gárgya the Brahman... impotent, in an assembly of the Yádavas... he engaged in arduous penance to obtain a son, who should be a terror to the tribe of Yadu... Kálayavana assembled many myriads of Mlechchhas... advanced impatiently against Mathurá.

title: Krishna Founds Dwaraka
one_line_summary: Fearing a two-front war with Jarasandha and Kalayavana, Krishna obtains twelve furlongs from the ocean and builds the fortified city of Dwaraka, conducting the Yadavas thither.
source_excerpt: Krishńa solicited a space of twelve furlongs from the ocean, and there he built the city of Dwáraka, defended by high ramparts... Thither Janárddana conducted the inhabitants of Mathurá.

title: Krishna Lures Kalayavana to Muchukunda
one_line_summary: Krishna flees unarmed from Kalayavana into Muchukunda's cave; the Yavana kicks the sleeping king, whose fiery glance consumes him to ashes, and Muchukunda praises Krishna as Vishnu.
source_excerpt: The rash Yavana entering the cave, and beholding a man lying asleep there, concluded it must be Krishńa, and kicked him; at which Muchukunda awoke, and casting on him an angry glance, the Yavana was instantly consumed, and reduced to ashes.

title: Krishna Seizes Kalayavana's Host
one_line_summary: Having destroyed Kalayavana by stratagem, Krishna captures his army of horses, elephants and cars, and delivers it to Ugrasena, freeing the Yadava race from fear of invasion.
source_excerpt: Krishńa having by this stratagem destroyed his enemy, returned to Mathurá, and took captive his army, rich in horses, elephants and cars, which he conducted to Dwáraká, and delivered to Ugrasena.

title: Balarama Revisits Vraja
one_line_summary: When hostilities cease, Balarama returns to Nanda's cow-pens, embraces the cowherds, and consoles the Gopis, who chide Krishna's inconstancy, with gentle messages from him.
source_excerpt: Baladeva... being desirous of seeing his kinsmen, went to Nanda's cow-pens, and there again conversed with the herdsmen and their females... Ráma consoled them by communicating to them agreeable, modest, affectionate, and gentle messages from Krishńa.

title: Balarama Drags the Yamuna
one_line_summary: Inebriated on wine from a Kadamba tree, Balarama commands the Yamuna to come to him and, when she refuses, drags her from her course with his ploughshare until she begs his pardon.
source_excerpt: Ráma in a rage took up his ploughshare, which he plunged into her bank, and dragged her to him, calling out, "Will you not come, you jade? will you not come?"... he compelled the dark river to quit its ordinary course.

title: Balarama Marries Revati
one_line_summary: Decorated by Lakshmi and sporting two months in Vraja, Balarama returns to Dwaraka and marries Revati, the daughter of king Raivata, by whom he has two sons.
source_excerpt: Thus decorated, Ráma sported two months in Vraja, and then returned to Dwáraká, where the married Revatí, the daughter of king Raivata, by whom he had two sons, Nishat́ha and Ulmuka.

title: Krishna Carries Off Rukmini
one_line_summary: Against her brother Rukmin's will, Krishna carries off the princess Rukmini on the eve of her betrothal to Sisupala, while Balarama and the Yadavas repel the pursuing princes.
source_excerpt: Hari contrived, on the eve of the nuptials, to carry off the princess, leaving Ráma and his kinsmen to sustain the weight of his enemies... Pauńd́raka... Śiśupála, Jarásandha... exerted themselves to kill Krishńa, but were repelled by Balaráma.

title: Krishna Overthrows but Spares Rukmin
one_line_summary: Rukmin, vowing never to return until he has slain Krishna, overtakes him; Krishna destroys his host and would kill him, but spares him at Rukmini's plea, and Rukmin founds the city Bhojakata.
source_excerpt: Krishńa destroyed with his discus... the host of Rukmin... and would have put him to death, but was withheld by the entreaties of Rukminí... 'He is my only brother... give me my brother in charity.'

title: Krishna Marries Rukmini and Pradyumna Is Born
one_line_summary: Krishna marries Rukmini by the Rakshasa rite; she bears him the gallant Pradyumna, a portion of the deity of love.
source_excerpt: After the defeat of Rukmin, Krishńa married Rukminí in due form, having first made her his own by the Rákshasa ritual. She bore him the gallant Pradyumna, a portion of the deity of love.

title: Sambara Steals the Infant Pradyumna
one_line_summary: Foreknowing the child will destroy him, the demon Sambara steals the six-day-old Pradyumna and casts him into the sea, where a great fish swallows him.
source_excerpt: When Pradyumna was but six days old, he was stolen from the lying-in chamber by Sambara, terrible as death; for the demon foreknew that Pradyumna, if he lived, would be his destroyer... cast him into the ocean.

title: Pradyumna Slays Sambara and Returns
one_line_summary: Rescued from the fish by Mayadevi, Pradyumna learns his birth, defeats Sambara's host, and slaying the enchanter with his own eighth illusion returns to Dwaraka with Mayavati.
source_excerpt: Seven times he foiled the delusions of the enchanter, and making himself master of the eighth, turned it against Sambara, and killed him... he proceeded to his father's house, where he alighted, along with Máyávatí, in the inner apartments.

title: The Nuptials of Aniruddha
one_line_summary: Pradyumna begets Aniruddha, who is betrothed to the granddaughter of Rukmin; the wedding is celebrated at Bhojakata in the presence of Krishna, Balarama and the Yadavas.
source_excerpt: he had by her the powerful and gallant prince Aniruddha... Upon the occasion of the nuptials Ráma and other Yádavas attended Krishńa to Bhojakat́a, the city of Rukmin.

title: Balarama Slays Rukmin at Dice
one_line_summary: At the wedding games, Rukmin cheats Balarama at dice and derides him; a heavenly voice confirms the foul play, and the enraged Balarama kills Rukmin and routs the assembled kings.
source_excerpt: Balaráma thus excited, his eyes red with rage, started up, and struck Rukmin with the board on which the game was played, and killed him.

title: Indra Reports the Tyranny of Naraka
one_line_summary: Indra comes to Dwaraka and tells Krishna how the demon Naraka has seized the maidens of the gods, Varuna's umbrella, Mandara's crest and Aditi's earrings, and now demands his elephant.
source_excerpt: The son of the earth, called Naraka, who rules over the city of Prágjyotisha, inflicts a great injury upon all creatures... He has taken away the umbrella of Varuńa... and the celestial nectar-dropping earrings of my mother Adití.

title: Krishna Slays Naraka and Frees the Captives
one_line_summary: Riding Garuda with Satyabhama, Krishna cuts Naraka's nooses, slays the demon and his host, and liberates sixteen thousand one hundred captive princesses, sending them to Dwaraka.
source_excerpt: when Naraka came into the field... the wielder of the discus... cut him in two with his celestial missile... In the apartments of the women he found sixteen thousand and one hundred damsels.

title: Krishna Restores Aditi's Earrings
one_line_summary: Krishna restores the recovered earrings to Aditi, who blesses him; Satyabhama is promised unfading beauty.
source_excerpt: on beholding Adití, paid his respects to her, along with Śakra; and, presenting to her her own earrings, informed her of the destruction of the demon Naraka.

title: Krishna Carries Off the Parijata Tree
one_line_summary: At Satyabhama's desire, Krishna uproots the celestial Parijata tree from Indra's garden and loads it upon Garuda, despite the protests of the garden keepers.
source_excerpt: Hari smiled upon her, and taking the Párijáta plant, put it upon Garud́a... 'This Párijáta tree belongs to Śachí... it is not proper, Govinda, for you to remove it.'

title: Krishna Defeats the Gods for the Parijata
one_line_summary: Indra and the gods attack to recover the Parijata tree; Krishna disarms them all with his discus and arrows, spares Indra, and the defeated king of gods acknowledges Krishna as the lord of the universe.
source_excerpt: Indra launched his bolt, but in vain, for Hari caught and arrested it... 'I am not ashamed of being vanquished by him who is the author of the creation, preservation, and destruction of the world.'

title: Krishna Plants the Parijata in Dwaraka
one_line_summary: With Indra's consent, Krishna carries the Parijata tree to Dwaraka and plants it in Satyabhama's garden, where its fragrance and sight reveal past births.
source_excerpt: Then alighting from Garud́a, he proceeded with Satyabhámá to her garden, and there planted the great Párijáta tree, the smell of which perfumed the earth for three furlongs, and an approach to which enabled every one to recollect the events of a prior existence.

title: Krishna Marries the Sixteen Thousand Princesses
one_line_summary: At an auspicious season Krishna multiplies himself into sixteen thousand one hundred forms and espouses every maiden rescued from Naraka, each believing him her single husband.
source_excerpt: at an auspicious season he espoused all the maidens whom Naraka had carried off... Sixteen thousand and one hundred was the number of the maidens, and into so many different forms did the foe of Madhu multiply himself.

title: Usha Dreams of Aniruddha
one_line_summary: Parvati foretells that Bana's daughter Usha will wed the man she sees in a dream; Aniruddha appears to her, and her friend Chitralekha paints the heroes until Usha recognises him.
source_excerpt: on that lunar day a youth appeared to Ushá in a dream, of whose person she became enamoured... the moment she beheld the picture of his son, the object of her passion, her eyes wide expanded... 'This is he! this is he!'

title: Bana Captures Aniruddha
one_line_summary: Chitralekha brings Aniruddha to Usha by magic; discovered, the prince slays Bana's guards but is bound in serpent bonds by the demon-king's illusions.
source_excerpt: The guards of the inner apartments discovering him there with Ushá, reported it to the king... Báňa... followed the counsel of his minister, and brought his magical faculties into the conflict, by which he succeeded in capturing the Yadu prince, and binding him in serpent bonds.

title: Krishna Battles Siva's Fever and Host
one_line_summary: Krishna, Balarama and Pradyumna fly on Garuda to Bana's city, where Krishna overcomes Siva's three-headed Fever and disables Siva with the weapon of yawning, putting Skanda to flight.
source_excerpt: Govinda, with the weapon of yawning, set Śankara a-gape... Hara, overcome with incessant gaping, sat down in his car, and was unable longer to contend with Krishńa... Kártikeya, wounded... took to flight.

title: Krishna Severs Bana's Arms and Spares Him
one_line_summary: In single combat Krishna cuts off Bana's thousand arms with his discus; when Siva pleads that he has granted Bana safety, Krishna spares the demon and rescues Aniruddha and Usha.
source_excerpt: The discus... lopped off successively the numerous arms of the Asura... 'Since you, Śankara, have given a boon unto Báňa, let him live: from respect to your promises, my discus is arrested.'

title: Krishna Destroys the False Vasudeva
one_line_summary: The impostor Paundraka, who has assumed Vishnu's emblems, demands Krishna's discus; Krishna marches on him and slays Paundraka and the king of Kasi, shooting the latter's head into his city.
source_excerpt: he let fly the discus and the mace, by which Pauńd́raka was cut to pieces, and cast on the ground... the valiant king of Káśí... continued the conflict, till Śauri decapitated him with his arrows, shooting his head into the city of Káśí.

title: Krishna's Discus Burns Benares
one_line_summary: The son of the slain king of Kasi conjures a fiery fiend against Krishna; his discus chases it back to Benares and consumes the city and its inhabitants in flames.
source_excerpt: Sudarśana, the discus of Vishńu, immediately attacked the fiend... pursued by him with equal velocity, until she reached Varánáśí... Thus was Varánáśí burnt, with all its princes and their followers... The whole of a city, that was inaccessible to the gods, was thus wrapped in flames.

title: Samba Carries Off Duryodhana's Daughter
one_line_summary: At her svayamvara, Samba, the son of Jambavati, carries off Duryodhana's daughter; pursued by the Kuru chiefs, he is defeated and taken prisoner, kindling Yadava wrath.
source_excerpt: At the choice of a husband by the daughter of Duryodhana, the princess was carried off by the hero Śámba, the son of Jámbavatí. Being pursued by Duryodhana, Karńa, Bhíshma, Drońa... he was defeated, and taken prisoner.

title: Balarama Drags Hastinapura
one_line_summary: When the Kauravas contemptuously refuse to release Samba, Balarama in wrath ploughs his weapon beneath Hastinapura's ramparts and drags the city until the terrified Kuru chiefs yield up Samba and his bride.
source_excerpt: the wielder of the club, Baladeva, his eyes red with rage, plunged the blade of his ploughshare downwards, beneath the ramparts of the city, and drew them towards him... the Kauravas delivered Śámba and his bride to the mighty Balaráma.

title: Balarama Slays the Ape Dwivida
one_line_summary: The ape-demon Dwivida, avenging Naraka, ravages the world and mocks Balarama in the groves of Raivata; Balarama fells him with a single blow of his fist.
source_excerpt: the monkey Dwivida came there, and stealing the ploughshare and the club of Baladeva, grinned at and mocked him... Bala replied with a blow of his fist upon the forehead of Dwivida, which felled him, vomiting blood, and lifeless, to the earth.

title: The Sages Curse the Yadavas
one_line_summary: Yadava boys dress Samba as a pregnant woman and mock the sages; the enraged sages pronounce that he shall bear an iron club that will crush the whole Yadava race.
source_excerpt: they dressed and adorned Sumba, the son of Jámbavatí, as a damsel... The sages... said, "She will bring forth a club, that shall crush the whole of the Yádava race."

title: Krishna Sends Uddhava to Badarikashrama
one_line_summary: Seeing the omens of Dwaraka's doom, Krishna bids Uddhava depart to the shrine of Naranarayana at Badarikashrama, where by meditating on Krishna he shall attain perfection.
source_excerpt: Do you go by a celestial route... to the holy place Badarikáśrama... and on that spot, sanctified by them, thou, by meditating on me, shalt obtain perfection through my favour.

title: The Yadavas Destroy One Another
one_line_summary: At Prabhasa the Yadava chiefs, inflamed by liquor, fall upon one another; the rushes in their hands become thunderbolts, and nearly the whole race perishes, even Krishna slaying many with an iron club.
source_excerpt: As they drank, the destructive flame of dissension was kindled amongst them... The rushes in their hands became like thunderbolts, and they struck one another with them fatal blows... In a short time there was not a single Yádava left alive, except the mighty Krishńa and Dáruka.

title: Sesha Departs from Balarama
one_line_summary: As Krishna watches, the great serpent Sesha issues from Balarama's mouth and enters the ocean, hymned by saints and serpents, and Ocean comes forth to receive him.
source_excerpt: Going towards Ráma, who was sitting at the root of a tree, they beheld a large serpent coming out of his mouth. Having issued from his mouth, the mighty snake proceeded towards the ocean... and entered into the waters of the deep.

title: Krishna Is Shot by the Hunter and Departs
one_line_summary: Seated in meditation, Krishna is struck in the sole by the hunter Jara's arrow tipped with the iron club's blade; he forgives the hunter and sends him to heaven, then abandons his mortal body.
source_excerpt: Then came there a hunter, named Jará, whose arrow was tipped with a blade made of the piece of iron of the club... beholding from a distance the foot of Krishńa, he mistook it for part of a deer, and shooting his arrow, lodged it in the sole... Then the illustrious Krishńa... abandoned his mortal body.

title: Arjuna Performs the Rites and Dwaraka Sinks
one_line_summary: Arjuna burns the bodies of Krishna and Rama; the eight queens with Rukmini and Revati enter the funeral fire, and the ocean rises to submerge the whole of Dwaraka.
source_excerpt: The eight queens of Krishńa... with Rukminí at their head, embraced the body of Hari, and entered the funeral fire... The ocean rose, and submerged the whole of Dwáraká, except alone the dwelling of the deity of the race of Yadu.

title: The Abhiras Rob Arjuna
one_line_summary: Leading Krishna's widowed wives and wealth from Dwaraka, Arjuna is set upon by Abhira robbers; his bow Gandiva goes slack, his weapons fail, and the thieves carry off the women and treasure.
source_excerpt: Thereupon Arjuna began to brace his heavenly bow Gándíva... but it was in vain; for, in spite of all his efforts to tighten it, it continued flaccid... the barbarians, in the sight of Arjuna, carried off all the women of the Vrishńi and Andhaka tribes.

title: Vyasa Consoles Arjuna and Parikshit Is Enthroned
one_line_summary: Vyasa tells Arjuna that Krishna's departure was the will of time and recounts Ashtavakra's curse on the Apsarasas; Arjuna installs Vajra in Mathura, and the Pandavas place Parikshit on the throne.
source_excerpt: Vyása replied to Arjuna, and said, "Think no more, my son, of your disgrace... Know that time subjects all beings to similar vicissitude." ...the sons of Páńd́u placed Paríkshit on the throne, and went to the forest.
